what: Okta sells identity software. It decides who is allowed to log in to a company's applications and systems, handling single sign-on, multi-factor authentication and the management of employee and customer accounts.
customers: Companies of all sizes managing employee access, and developers using Auth0 to handle logins for their own apps.
money: identity platform subscriptions for workforce and customer identity
moat: Independence from the big cloud vendors, so it connects to everything, combined with integrations into thousands of applications that make it the hub of access control.
risks: Microsoft bundles competing identity tools with its enterprise licences at little extra cost
Growth has slowed from its earlier pace
Security breaches at an identity vendor are especially damaging, and it has had them
Analyst targets imply the shares are roughly fairly valued
opportunities: Revenue grew about 12% last year with a 77% gross margin
Cash of about $2.3 billion against almost no debt
Identity governance and privileged access are newer products that raise spending per customer
watch: Remaining performance obligations and net revenue retention.
